before: The appointment came with a seal, a coat, and a list. The list is the company: ten names from three regions, owed to Ironwake under the armistice. None of them has arrived. I read it every morning anyway. So far it is the only part of the job I have done.

The keep is two days east. Someone has followed me since the ford, and the waystation ahead has a fort with its gate still on. A fort keeps the weather off. It does not keep anyone from shooting at it.
What the crown taught me before it sent me, which was not a lot: read the blow before you swing it. Know who answers back and who cannot. A sword answers a sword. It does not answer a bow.

after: Three dead on a road nobody will remember. I have nobody to add to the list yet, which is its own kind of report.
The waystation keeper says a Kestrow chaplain bound for Ironwake was taken off the mill road two days back. Her name is on my list. East it is, by way of the mill.
